elaine: Quick heads-up — I pushed a tiny follow-up to the SDK examples PR that reorganizes the cross‑lang streaming + pagination snippets. need a quick pair of 👀 before i merge. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/docs/pulls/842

mike: On it. which files changed?

elaine: docs/sdks/python/streaming.md, docs/sdks/ts/streams.md, docs/sdks/go/pagination.md. also renamed the param in examples from continuation_token -> cursor to match runtime.

sarah: thanks — i remember we purposely used continuation_token in older guides to be explicit. are we sure cursor is the canonical name across SDKs?

omar: quick check: runtime API uses `cursor` in the JSON payload. SDK bindings map that to `cursor` for TS/Go and `cursor` for Python generator helpers as well. i'd prefer consistency.

elaine: yep, runtime uses cursor. this PR also fixes a streaming example that forgot to call `await response.aclose()` in python async iterator (leaks).

mike: can you paste the problematic snippet here? easier to eyeball.

elaine: sure — current snippet in PR (python) is:
```python
async def stream_responses():
    resp = await client.stream.create(model="redwood-small", input="...", max_tokens=100)
    async for chunk in resp.[1mgenerate[0m():
        print(chunk.text)
```
which misses closing the stream explicitly. changed to:
```python
async def stream_responses():
    resp = await client.stream.create(model="redwood-small", input="...", max_tokens=100)
    try:
        async for chunk in resp.generate():
            print(chunk.text)
    finally:
        await resp.aclose()
```

omar: good call. also suggest adding a small note about backpressure and not awaiting inside the loop for heavy workloads.

sarah: for TypeScript we had a similar anti-pattern where examples `await` every chunk which serializes processing. updated TS snippet to use nonblocking handlers:
```ts
const stream = await client.stream.create({...})
for await (const part of stream) {
  // queue to worker pool instead of await(process(part))
  workerQueue.push(part)
}
await stream.close()
```

mike: nice. is `close()` the JS equivalent of `aclose()`? we should call out naming differences in the docs page.

elaine: yes — TS uses `close()` on the async iterable wrapper, Go uses `Close()` on the stream object. i've added a short table at the top: Python -> aclose(), TS -> close(), Go -> Close().

docs-bot: [auto] Added checklist item: update SDK changelog links and runtime param docs.

mike: small nit — in docs/sdks/go/pagination.md the Go paginator example still had `continuationToken` in the struct. i left a review comment with the exact line.

elaine: saw that, fixed in a follow-up commit. Go example now:
```go
req := &inference.PaginateRequest{
    Model: "redwood-small",
    Cursor: "",
    PageSize: 50,
}
for {
    resp, err := client.Paginate(ctx, req)
    if err != nil { break }
    for _, item := range resp.Items { fmt.Println(item.Id) }
    if resp.Cursor == "" { break }
    req.Cursor = resp.Cursor
}
```

omar: perfect. also added a small blurb on retry idempotency for pagination endpoints — page tokens should be treated as opaque and retried safely, but avoid retrying with changed page_size.

sarah: can we add a quick test snippet (pseudo) that shows retry/backoff usage with our SDK helpers? good to have one-liner pattern for folks.

elaine: added this to the python page under "Retries":
```python
from redwood import RetryPolicy
policy = RetryPolicy(max_attempts=5, backoff="exponential")
with client.with_retry(policy):
    resp = client.paginate.list(...)
```

mike: looks good. small doclink fix: the pagination.md referenced an old internal RFC link — updated to the public runtime spec: https://docs.redwood.ai/runtime/pagination

elaine: thanks — i'm going to merge after one more approving review. anyone else want to glance at the TS/Go sync/async naming table?

omar: lgtm from infra side.

sarah: approved from DX. left a tiny grammar fix.

mike: approved — merging. :shipit:

elaine: merged. will follow up with a separate PR to add test-case snippets for backpressure and worker pools. thanks y'all! :tada!
